note.explanation: Responsible computer usage means choosing suitable, secure hardware and software and using technology thoughtfully. Check that your equipment is safe, efficient for your tasks, and compatible with the programs you need.
examples: A computer without updated antivirus software may be more at risk from viruses or hackers.
An old computer may run a new video game slowly or may not run it at all.
note.checkAnswer: Check the software's system requirements and compare them with your computer's specifications.
note.simple: Choose computer parts and programs that are safe, suit your task, and work well together.
note.checkQuestion: What should you compare to check whether software will work on your computer?
note.title: Choosing and using computer technology responsibly
steps: Identify what you need the computer to do.
Choose hardware and software suitable for that task.
Check the software's system requirements against your computer's specifications.
Use updated, secure software to help protect your information.
note.answer: Responsible computer usage includes protecting personal information, making wise choices about hardware and software, and behaving respectfully and ethically online.

options: Compare the program's system requirements with the computer's specifications.
Choose the computer with the brightest screen.
Install the program without checking the computer.
Choose the program with the largest number of features.
mcqs.stem: A student wants to install a program. What is the best way to check whether it will work with the computer?
rationales: This is correct because checking system requirements against specifications helps ensure compatibility.
Screen brightness does not show whether a program is compatible.
Installing without checking may result in software that does not work properly.
The number of features does not establish compatibility with the computer.

options: Use software from an unknown source because it is new.
Keep security software updated and avoid insecure or outdated programs.
Turn off all security features to make the computer easier to use.
Use any software even if it does not suit the computer.
mcqs.stem: Which choice best supports safer computer use?
rationales: Unknown software may be unsafe, so choosing it does not support safer use.
This is correct because updated security software can help protect against viruses and other risks.
Turning off security features can leave the computer more exposed to risks.
Software that does not suit the computer may not work properly and is not a wise choice.

options: Hardware means programs, while software means physical parts.
Hardware and software both mean online accounts.
Hardware means physical computer parts, while software means programs and applications.
Hardware means websites, while software means computer cables.
mcqs.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes hardware from software?
rationales: This reverses the meanings of hardware and software.
Neither term means online accounts.
This is correct: hardware is physical equipment, and software consists of programs and applications.
Websites and cables do not give the correct meanings of these terms.

options: It makes all computer tasks happen instantly.
It guarantees that no computer risk can occur.
It helps tasks run more smoothly and makes the computer suitable for the user's needs.
It removes the need to check software requirements.
mcqs.stem: Why should a user choose hardware and software that suit the tasks they need to do?
rationales: Suitable choices do not make every task instant.
No choice can guarantee that every computer risk is eliminated.
This is correct because suitable choices can improve efficiency and the overall computer experience.
Requirements still need to be checked to make sure hardware and software are compatible.

options: A computer's specifications and the software's system requirements.
The colour of the computer and the software's icon.
The computer's location and the program's name.
The number of people who use the computer.
mcqs.stem: Which two details are most useful when checking hardware and software compatibility?
rationales: This is correct because compatibility is checked by matching system requirements with computer specifications.
Colour and icon design do not show whether the software can run on the computer.
Location and program name do not establish compatibility.
The number of users does not show whether the software matches the computer's specifications.

options: Use any computer, even if it is broken or unsafe.
Select hardware and software thoughtfully, considering safety, efficiency, and compatibility.
Choose software only because it is popular.
Ignore whether hardware and software work together.
mcqs.stem: Which action is the best example of responsible computer use when choosing technology?
rationales: Using broken or unsafe equipment ignores the need to use technology safely.
This is correct because responsible choices consider safety, efficiency, and compatibility.
Popularity alone does not show whether software is suitable, safe, or compatible.
Ignoring compatibility can lead to software and hardware that do not work well together.

written.text: Q11.1. What is the importance of using computers safely and responsibly?
written.finalAnswer: It protects personal information and helps us make wise choices about hardware and software.

rubric.why: Protecting personal information is a key reason to use computers safely.
rubric.description: State that responsible use protects personal information.

rubric.why: The answer should also show what responsible use involves.
rubric.description: Give the correct final answer about responsible choices.
rubric.how: Mention wise choices about hardware and software or safe and responsible use.

modelAnswer: Safe and responsible computer use helps protect our personal information.
It also helps us make wise choices about the hardware and software we use.
Therefore, it helps us use computers safely and responsibly.

written.text: Q11.2. How does choosing the right hardware and software affect your computer usage?
written.finalAnswer: The right hardware and software can improve safety, efficiency, compatibility, and the overall computer experience.

rubric.why: The textbook identifies safety and efficiency as effects of suitable choices.
rubric.description: Explain at least one benefit such as safety or efficiency.
rubric.how: State that suitable choices support safer or more efficient computer use.

rubric.why: Compatibility and the overall experience complete the explanation.
rubric.description: Give the correct final answer about the effects of suitable choices.
rubric.how: Mention compatibility or how hardware and software affect the user's experience.

modelAnswer: The right hardware and software can make computer use safer.
They can help users complete tasks quickly and easily.
When they work well together, they improve compatibility and the overall computer experience.

written.text: Q11.3. Why is it important to use antivirus software on your computer?
written.finalAnswer: Antivirus software helps prevent viruses and other digital threats that could harm the computer or put information at risk.

rubric.why: Preventing digital viruses is the main safety point in the section.
rubric.description: State that antivirus software helps prevent viruses.
rubric.how: Use a phrase such as prevent viruses or protect against viruses.

rubric.why: The answer should connect antivirus use with reducing harm or protecting information.
rubric.description: Give the correct final answer about the reason for antivirus software.
rubric.how: Explain that viruses or hackers could harm the device or put information at risk.

modelAnswer: Viruses can harm a computer, and insecure devices can make it easier for viruses or hackers to steal information.
Antivirus software helps prevent digital viruses.
Therefore, using antivirus software helps protect the computer and its information.

written.text: Q11.4. What are some examples of good practices when selecting hardware and software?
written.finalAnswer: Choose hardware and software suited to your tasks, use secure and updated software, and check system requirements against the computer's specifications.

rubric.why: Checking requirements against specifications is the section's stated compatibility practice.
rubric.how: Say to check the system requirements and compare them with computer specifications.

rubric.why: Good choices should also suit the task and support safe, efficient use.
rubric.description: Give the correct final answer with another good selection practice.
rubric.how: Mention choosing suitable hardware or software and considering safety or efficiency.

modelAnswer: Choose hardware and software that suit the tasks you need to do.
Use secure and updated software.
Check the software's system requirements and match them with the computer's specifications.

written.text: Q11.5. How can choosing compatible hardware and software enhance your computer experience?
written.finalAnswer: Compatible hardware and software work well together, helping programs run properly and making computer use more effective and less frustrating.

rubric.why: Compatibility means the hardware and software work well together.
rubric.description: Explain what compatible hardware and software do.
rubric.how: State that they work well together.

rubric.why: The answer should describe how compatibility benefits the user's experience.
rubric.description: Give the correct final answer about the benefit of compatibility.
rubric.how: Explain that programs can work properly and computer use can be more effective.

modelAnswer: Compatible hardware and software work well together.
This helps programs work properly instead of being slow or not working at all.
Therefore, compatible choices make computer use more effective and improve the overall experience.

written.text: Q11.1. 1. Discuss the importance of responsible computer usage in today's digital world. Explain how selecting the right hardware and software can affect safety, efficiency, and compatibility in computer use.
written.finalAnswer: Responsible computer usage protects personal information and supports respectful, ethical use. Choosing suitable hardware and software supports safety, helps tasks be completed quickly and easily, and ensures compatibility when system requirements match the computer's specifications.

rubric.why: The response needs to explain why responsible computer use matters.
rubric.description: Explain the importance of responsible use.
rubric.how: Mention protecting personal information and using computers safely and responsibly.

rubric.why: The section connects appropriate and secure technology choices with safety.
rubric.description: Explain the safety effect of choosing suitable hardware and software.
rubric.how: Refer to safe or updated technology and how it helps reduce risks.

rubric.why: Efficiency is a named benefit and should be explained, not just listed.
rubric.how: State that suitable choices help users complete tasks quickly and easily.

rubric.why: Compatibility is the third named factor, and the section gives a way to check it.
rubric.description: Give the correct final answer about compatibility and selection.
rubric.how: Explain that hardware and software should work well together and that requirements should match specifications.

modelAnswer: Responsible computer usage means protecting personal information, making wise choices about hardware and software, and behaving respectfully and ethically online.
The right hardware and software can improve safety; outdated or insecure technology can put users at risk.
Suitable hardware and software help users complete tasks quickly and easily, improving efficiency.
Compatibility means that hardware and software work well together.
Check the software's system requirements and match them with the computer's specifications.
Thus, responsible use and suitable technology help make computer use safer, more efficient, and compatible.

examTips: This section can be tested through short questions asking for the importance of responsible computer use, the effects of choosing hardware and software, or the meaning of compatibility.
A long question may ask you to discuss responsible computer usage and explain safety, efficiency, and compatibility.
For full marks, explain each factor rather than only listing its name. For compatibility, include checking software system requirements against computer specifications.
Use the textbook's terms: hardware is physical computer parts; software is programs and applications.

hints: Think about how a program and a computer must work together.
State the compatibility check given in the section: compare software requirements with computer specifications.

explain.title: Responsible computer use
explain.body: Safe and responsible computer usage means knowing how to protect personal information, making wise choices about the hardware and software we use, and ensuring that our online behavior is respectful and ethical.

explain.title: Hardware and software
explain.body: Hardware refers to the physical parts like the monitor, keyboard, and CPU, while software includes the programs and applications we use, such as word processors or games.

explain.title: Safety and efficiency
explain.body: The right hardware and software can help keep computer use safer and help you complete tasks quickly and easily. Outdated or insecure technology can put you at risk.

explain.title: Compatibility
explain.body: Compatibility means that the hardware and software should work well together. Check the software's system requirements and match them with the computer's specifications.

mistakes: Do not confuse hardware with software: hardware is the physical equipment; software is programs and applications.
Do not say compatibility is about the colour, price, or brand of a device; explain that the hardware and software should work well together.
Do not forget to mention checking system requirements against the computer's specifications.
Do not describe efficiency only as speed; the section says suitable choices help users complete tasks quickly and easily.
Do not assume old or insecure software is safe; the section warns that it can put users at risk.
